text: Zik woke before dawn to silence.
speaker: Narrator

text: Real silence—the kind the desert had not offered since they found the staircase. No wind moved across the dunes. No night birds called. Even the donkeys stood still, ears down, as if holding their breath with him.
speaker: Narrator

text: He lay beneath his blanket and listened for the knocking. Nothing came.
speaker: Narrator

text: Slowly he reached for the journal. The cover was colder than the desert night had any right to leave it. He opened it anyway. No new lines. The pages sat exactly as he had left them. The mark on his palm had gone cold too. For the first time since the tomb it looked like nothing more than an old scar catching the wrong light.
speaker: Narrator

text: For one treacherous second he let himself believe it was over.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then he checked his father's compass. The needle no longer pointed into the earth. It pointed back toward Uruk—steady, almost eager.
speaker: Narrator

text: He did not trust it. He got up anyway.
speaker: Narrator

text: He woke Balag first. The big man cracked one eye open.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag did not argue. He looked toward the staircase, said nothing, and started rolling his blanket. That silence frightened Zik more than any argument would have.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun agreed before he finished the sentence. She had slept badly; the hollows under her eyes showed it. Enhedu said nothing at all. Her silence had teeth.
speaker: Narrator

text: They broke camp in the dark and put their backs to the ridge.
speaker: Narrator

text: For the first few hours the desert played along. The sky went from black to bruised purple to the flat white of morning. Heat crawled up out of the sand in waves you could watch. Their shadows stretched long and blue, then shrank beneath them as the sun climbed. Zik navigated by the old caravan markers and his father's map, the same way he always had.
speaker: Narrator

text: The first marker was exactly where it should have been.
speaker: Narrator

text: He stopped beside a half-buried stone pillar, worn smooth by centuries of wind, and traced the carved symbol with two fingers. Old work. Older than the outpost. But the direction it pointed was plain enough to read without translation.

text: The well should have been less than an hour ahead. Zik remembered its position the way he remembered debts: the angle of the dunes, the low ridge of black stone to the south, the broken track leading into the basin. He had marked it twice.
speaker: Narrator

text: They reached the place the map, the sun, and four separate memories agreed it should be.
speaker: Narrator

text: Flat sand stretched unbroken to the horizon. No depression. No shadow of what had once been a well. The location itself had simply ceased to exist.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag turned in a slow circle.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun had already taken sightings off the sun and the ridgeline.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The desert has stopped agreeing with itself.
speaker: Ninsun

text: They found the well again when the sun stood directly overhead, throwing no shadows at all. It sat several miles off their line of travel, in a place none of them remembered crossing. The stones around its mouth were wet.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik stopped at the edge of the basin. Water sat inside, dark and glass-still. He could smell it from ten feet off—iron, old blood, and a taste underneath both that he did not have a word for and did not want one.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag took a step toward it.
